title: Recovering Missing Children Act
official_summary:
(This measure has not been amended since it was passed by the House on May 10, 2016. The summary of that version is repeated here.)

Recovering Missing Children Act

(Sec. 2) This bill amends the Internal Revenue Code to permit federal law enforcement officials to seek an ex parte order in federal court for the disclosure of tax returns or return information for criminal investigations pertaining to missing or exploited children.

If the order is granted, the information may be disclosed to federal officers and employees who are personally and directly engaged in judicial or administrative proceedings, investigations, or federal grand jury proceedings to enforce a federal criminal statute pertaining to a missing or exploited child.

A federal agency may disclose to state and local law enforcement agencies information obtained under the authority provided by this bill if:

  • the state or local agency is part of a team with the federal agency in the investigation, and
  • the information is disclosed only to officers and employees who are personally and directly engaged in the investigation.

The state or local agency may only use the disclosed information in locating the missing child, in a grand jury proceeding, or in any preparation for, or investigation which may result in, a judicial or administrative proceeding.

summary.headline: This law lets federal investigators get court orders to see tax return information when investigating crimes involving missing or exploited children.
summary.what_it_does: The law changes the Internal Revenue Code so federal law enforcement can ask a federal court, without notifying the taxpayer first, for an order allowing disclosure of tax returns or related information in criminal investigations about missing or exploited children. If a judge grants the order, federal officers and employees directly involved in related proceedings may receive that information. Federal agencies may also share it with state and local police who are working on a joint team with them, but only for locating the child or for related legal proceedings.

who_it_affects.group: Children who are missing or exploited
who_it_affects.how: Federal investigators may be able to use tax return information in their efforts to find them and pursue criminal cases.

who_it_affects.group: Taxpayers whose returns could be disclosed
who_it_affects.how: Their tax return information may be shared with investigators if a federal judge approves a request in a qualifying child-related criminal case.

who_it_affects.group: Federal law enforcement officers and agencies
who_it_affects.how: They gain a court-order process to obtain tax return information for criminal investigations involving missing or exploited children.

who_it_affects.group: State and local law enforcement agencies on joint federal teams
who_it_affects.how: They may receive shared tax return information from federal agencies, but only for specific investigative and legal purposes.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted on June 30, 2016, and the summary does not list a separate effective date.
